However, I can't reproduce. ``` jb@unu:~ $ pwd /Users/jb jb@unu:~ $ ls -ld t? drwxr-xr-x 4 jb staff 128 Sep 7 08:10 t1/ lrwxr-xr-x 1 jb staff 2 Sep 7 08:09 t2@ -> t1 ``` I suspect this is something specific to symlinks on Windows, which makes it out of my immediate jurisdiction... Exact details on the setup and error message may help.

Just to clarify, the symlinks were generated with "mklink /d [source] [destination]". The symlink was pointed to two different drives, I didn't test a symlink on the same drive but I assume that's highly unlikely to be related to the issue.
